findings.title: Adding abstract order() breaks binary compatibility for existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: CryptoProvider is a public interface that external integrations may implement and compile against older Keycloak versions. Adding an abstract method `int order()` makes existing provider JARs binary-incompatible: ServiceLoader will instantiate them, and the method reference `CryptoProvider::order` used in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider will throw AbstractMethodError because the implementation class lacks that method. Keep binary compatibility by making `order()` a default method, for example `default int order() { return 0; }`.

findings.title: Equal provider order values make provider selection nondeterministic
findings.body: detectProvider now sorts providers only by `order` descending and silently picks the first one. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, and ServiceLoader encounter order for equal priority is not specified. If more than one of these providers is on the classpath, the selected crypto implementation becomes arbitrary and can change between runs or environments, replacing the previous fail-fast behavior. Assign distinct order values or add a deterministic tie-breaker.

findings.title: readSequence can loop forever on a zero-length child element
findings.body: `readSequence` loops while `length > 0` and decrements `length` by `bytes.length`. `readNext()` can return a zero-length byte array when a child TLV has content length 0, which is valid ASN.1 DER for some primitive types. If that happens, `length` is never decremented and this loop spins forever. The decoder is used to parse DER-encoded ECDSA signatures, so a malicious or malformed signature can cause CPU exhaustion or denial of service. Reject zero-length TLV children in this path or decrement by the number of header bytes consumed separately.

findings.title: Registered CryptoProvider throws UnsupportedOperationException for core signing operations
findings.body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider is registered through META-INF/services and becomes the active CryptoProvider when no higher-order provider exists. However `getSignature` and many other required CryptoProvider methods throw UnsupportedOperationException. Keycloak's JWS signing path calls `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getSignature(algorithm)`, so client authentication or token handling that requires signing will fail at runtime when this provider is selected. The added test only exercises ASN.1 conversion directly and does not exercise provider selection or JWS signing, so this regression is not covered. Either implement the needed methods or do not register this class as a general CryptoProvider.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an unrelated default KeyStore provider
findings.body: The CryptoProvider contract describes `getBouncyCastleProvider()` as returning the BouncyCastle (or FIPS BouncyCastle) provider. This implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is normally a JDK provider such as SunJCE/SunJSSE and has no relation to BouncyCastle. Callers that rely on BC algorithms or provider identity will get incorrect behavior. Returning null, as WildFlyElytronProvider does, or actually loading/registering BouncyCastle would be consistent with the interface.
